chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Awn ibn Jarir, from Umar ibn Harun al-Thaq-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'All locusts are halal (permissible to eat), and as for what dies in the sea, do not eat it.'

key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: Permissible/Halal (specifically implying no special slaughter is required)

ai.seo_question: Are all locusts considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Tusi’s Tahdhib, establishes the permissibility of locusts as 'dhaki' (fully permissible) without requiring ritual slaughter, a ruling unique among land animals in Shia jurisprudence. It contrasts this with marine creatures, prohibiting the consumption of those that die naturally in the sea, thereby distinguishing between living catch and dead marine life. This distinction highlights the specific legal status of locusts as an exception to the general rule of slaughter for terrestrial animals.
